english.notes: (i) This offence is not committed where the cat lives or lived in the same household as the accused. See section 2(2) of the Pet Abduction Act 2024 for details.(ii) Section 2(3) of the Act contains a defence for the individual charged with the offence to show that they had lawful authority or a reasonable excuse for the taking of the cat. Section 2(4) states that they are taken to have shown the defence if they have adduced sufficient evidence to raise an issue in respect of the defence and the contrary was not proved beyond reasonable doubt. See section 2 for full details of defences.(iii) References to the 'taking of a cat' include causing or inducing the cat to accompany a person or causing the cat to be taken (section 2(6)).

other.penalty: Either waySummary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and/or a fine. The maximum penalty on summary conviction may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 2(5) of the Pet Abduction Act 2024 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022. Time limit for prosecutions: None
